encounters.cc: Irregular, heavy menstrual bleeding for 6 months requiring frequent pad changes, now with 2 months amenorrhea and spotting

lines: Irregular, heavy menstrual bleeding for 6 months requiring frequent pad changes, now with 2 months amenorrhea and spotting
She reports that her menstrual cycles have been unpredictable, with intervals ranging from 21 to 45 days, and the bleeding is often so heavy that she has to change her sanitary pads every 1-2 hours.
She has not had a menstrual period for the past 2 months but has experienced spotting over the last week.
Her past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic retinopathy
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 15 years ago (20 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Social (1-2 glasses of wine weekly).
She has a BMI of 35 kg/m^2. On physical examination, her blood pressure is 142/90 mmHg.
A bimanual pelvic exam reveals an enlarged, nontender uterus without adnexal masses.
No cervical lesions or discharge is noted.

She has not seen an ophthalmologist in over 10 years.
Her current medications include metformin and insulin glargine.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic retinopathy
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 15 years ago (20 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Social (1-2 glasses of wine weekly).
Physical examination reveals decreased visual acuity bilaterally and no focal neurological deficits.

encounters.cc: Bilateral knee pain with activity for 6 months, morning stiffness lasting 20 minutes

lines: Bilateral knee pain with activity for 6 months, morning stiffness lasting 20 minutes

This 58-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, central diabetes insipidus, and history of endometrial carcinoma presents to Rheumatology following prior ophthalmology and oncology care.
She reports a 6-month history of bilateral knee pain that worsens with activity and improves with rest.
She notes morning stiffness lasting approximately 20 minutes.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with metformin.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic retinopathy
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 15 years ago (20 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Social (1-2 glasses of wine weekly).
On physical examination, there is no erythema or warmth, but there is bony enlargement of both knee joints with tenderness on palpation.
There is no effusion, and the range of motion is preserved but painful at the extremes.
Radiographs of the knees show joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophyte formation.

encounters.cc: Routine health maintenance examination with no acute complaints

lines: Routine health maintenance examination with no acute complaints

The patient is a 59-year-old female with a 14-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, central diabetes insipidus, and history of endometrial carcinoma who previously presented with diabetic retinopathy and osteoarthritis.
She returns for routine health maintenance and reports no acute complaints today.
She has a history of hypertension, controlled with lisinopril, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with metformin.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic retinopathy
Her daughter accompanies her but has to leave early for work.
The patient's vital signs are within normal limits, and her BMI is 31 kg/m^2.
On physical examination, you note no abnormalities except for mild acanthosis nigricans around the neck.
The patient appears anxious and has difficulty understanding your explanation of the procedure due to her limited English proficiency.
You consider the best way to communicate effectively with the patient to obtain informed consent for the breast examination.
You decide to perform a breast examination as part of the routine check-up.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of progressive lip and tongue swelling over several hours without urticaria or respiratory distress

lines: Sudden onset of progressive lip and tongue swelling over several hours without urticaria or respiratory distress
This patient with Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and endometrial cancer presents to the Emergency Department.
She reports waking this morning with the swelling, which has progressively worsened over the past few hours.
She denies any associated urticaria, pruritus, or respiratory distress.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes lisinopril, and type 2 diabetes mellitus controlled with metformin.
She has been on lisinopril for 2 years.
She has no known drug allergies
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic retinopathy
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 15 years ago (20 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Social (1-2 glasses of wine weekly).
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 beats per minute.
There is noticeable non-pitting edema of the lips and tongue without erythema or warmth.
The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.
- Complete blood count: within normal limits

lines: 2-day history of headache, nausea, and confusion following recent desmopressin dose increase
This patient with diabetes insipidus and endometrial carcinoma presents with headache, nausea, and confusion.
She notes symptom onset shortly after her endocrinologist increased desmopressin dose for persistent polyuria and polydipsia.
Her medications include metformin, lisinopril, and desmopressin.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic retinopathy
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 15 years ago (20 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Social (1-2 glasses of wine weekly).
Her blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute
On physical examination, she is oriented to person only.
Her mucous membranes are moist, and there is no peripheral edema.

encounters.cc: Acute onset of severe shortness of breath, orthopnea, and palpitations beginning 2 hours ago while gardening

lines: Acute onset of severe shortness of breath, orthopnea, and palpitations beginning 2 hours ago while gardening

This patient with diabetes, hypertension, prior cancer, and SIADH presents to the emergency department with acute onset of shortness of breath, orthopnea, and palpitations beginning 2 hours ago while gardening
- Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH) (diagnosed 2024-07-15)
She has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic retinopathy
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 15 years ago (20 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Social (1-2 glasses of wine weekly).
On examination, she is tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg, and heart rate of 110 beats per minute.
Auscultation of the lungs reveals bilateral rales halfway up both lung fields.
Cardiac examination shows a new holosystolic murmur at the apex that radiates to the axilla.
Chest X-ray demonstrates pulmonary venous congestion and interstitial edema.
The electrocardiogram shows sinus tachycardia with no ST-segment changes.

encounters.cc: 3-month history of intermittent vaginal bleeding in a patient with prior endometrial carcinoma

lines: 3-month history of intermittent vaginal bleeding in a patient with prior endometrial carcinoma
The patient returns to Obstetrics and Gynecology six years after her initial endometrial carcinoma diagnosis.
She reports a 3-month history of intermittent vaginal bleeding.
Her last menstrual period was 6 years ago.
She denies associated pelvic pain, weight loss, or bowel habit changes.
- Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH) (diagnosed 2024-07-15)
No family history of gynecologic cancers
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 15 years ago (20 pack-year history).
Alcohol: Social (1-2 glasses of wine weekly).
Blood pressure is 132/86 mmHg, and her BMI is 31 kg/m^2
A pelvic examination reveals a small amount of blood in the vaginal vault, but no masses are palpable, and the uterus is of normal size.
No adnexal tenderness or masses are noted.
